newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end higher, led by silver.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end higher, led by silver.

text.p: New York precious metals futures ended higher Thursday, led by a strong rally in silver, but not before gold saw new 40-month lows early.

"There's been a dramatic outperformance by silver over gold in recent weeks, leading to talk of some large spread plays between the two metals, but the market remains very short and sentiment is still bearish overall," fund manager Jeff Kowal of Friedberg Mercantile Group in Toronto said.
COMEX March silver ended up 15.2 cents at $4.875 an ounce after recovering from a session low of $4.710. Estimated total volume in silver futures was 27,000 lots.
March silver ended above its 55-day (quarterly) moving average for the first time since August 1995, suggesting the year-long downtrend may be nearing an end, analysts said.
Silver has refused to follow gold lower since the start of 1997, and the spot gold/silver ratio slid below last August's low at 73.71 intraday, before ending at 72.27, an eight month low.
Meanwhile, COMEX February gold closed up $0.80 at $352.50, but not before setting a new life-of-contract low of $347.30. Total estimated gold futures volume was a high 85,000 contracts.

In the bullion market, spot gold ended the session quoted at $351.25/75 compared to the London afternoon fix of $348.00, which was a fresh 40-month low. Spot gold closed in New York Wednesday around $350.50/$351.00.
However, some fund shortcovering and rolling of positions into forward months was providing support on the dips in gold futures, traders said.
In data released Thursday, open interest in COMEX February gold fell 7,656 lots Wednesday, while open interest in April gold rose 3,771 lots and total gold open interest fell 3,588 lots to 201,883.
Total open interest in silver futures fell 416 lots to 92,807 contracts.
The market remains concerned about the potential for further European central bank sales though, traders said.
Also weighing on the market is the possibility of producer hedging, after gold fell below $350 an ounce as the US dollar soared this week.
The dollar saw a new 47-month high against yen Thursday, after seeing 31-month highs against the mark this week also.
The COMEX April platinum/gold spread was little changed Thursday around $5.60 an ounce, as NYMEX April platinum ended up $0.70 at $360.20 after hitting a new life-of-contract low of $357.50 early.
NYMEX March palladium, which has been in an uptrend since early December, closed up five cents at $123.60.

"Unsettled contract negotiations between Russia and Japanese fabricators reportedly are forcing a number of Japanese fabricators to turn to the spot palladium market for this metal," CPM Group analyst Edward Kempf said.
"This action has been supporting palladium prices in recent weeks."
